what_happened: The job to measure tokens loaded per class of work in athena status was rejected at the final verdict. One of 6 acceptance criteria was unmet: running cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test as separate commands (or pointing to Athena-recorded passes on the final tree), all passing. The verifier gave one major finding and no blockers: behavior criterion 5 is unmet because its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43). The test check also failed separately: shard 3 of 6 reported 1 of 13 units failed (athena-cli --test drain). The kept output shows only the passing setup tests, so the failing drain test and its assertion are not visible.
cause: The test check's kept output is only the tail of a different, passing test binary plus the shard summary line. The failing drain test's name and assertion are not retained. The producer, the verifier and the the person running Athena therefore cannot tell whether the new status measure broke drain or the failure is unrelated. Nothing extracts the failing test's output from the shard log, and no baseline run shows whether the failure predates the job. The same new-status-measure job family is also repeatedly rejected on D43 evidence.
other_causes: The producer's behavior evidence did not cite commands that ran (D43), and nothing checked this before the final verdict.
A job that adds an always-printed line to status output may break existing tests that read that output, such as the drain test, and nothing runs those tests earlier (class 20261111-111854-e6vm).
open_hypotheses: The drain test failure may have been caused by the new status output (tokens per class of work) rather than being pre-existing or flaky.
The failure could be an intermittent test unrelated to the job, since the fields give no baseline.
The unmet fmt/clippy/test criterion may be unmet only because the test check failed, not because of any separate fmt or clippy problem.
contradictions: The criterion for fmt, clippy and test is listed as unmet, but gate_counts shows 2 fmt ends and 2 clippy ends in total, and no fmt or clippy check is listed as failed here. Only the test check failed.
prevention: Add a code check that, when a test shard fails, keeps the failing test's name and assertion output (the lines around 'FAILED' or 'panicked') as the check's kept output, and runs the failing test once on the base tree to record whether it failed before the job. Also have the producer run the affected existing tests (here athena-cli --test drain) before finishing. That makes the cause of a failed test visible to everyone, and it separates failures the job caused from ones it did not.
proposed_request: Make the test check's kept output show why a test shard failed. When a shard reports failed units, keep the failing test names and their assertion or panic messages instead of the tail of the last passing binary. Also record whether the same test fails on the base tree. Then re-run the job that measures tokens loaded per class of work in athena status, and make sure athena-cli --test drain passes with the new status output. Acceptance: (1) a test with a deliberately failing unit produces kept output that names the test and its assertion; (2) the kept output for a passing shard is unchanged; (3) cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test pass; (4) the CHANGELOG.md entry is added.
